pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Wizards preview:  Round two against the Wizards
pistons.body:
The Pistons and Wizards play each other again, but it is after 3 days of rest for the Pistons and the day after a game for the Wizards because the NBA used Chat GPT to generate the schedule this year or something.  This will only be the Pistons 3rd game in the last 8 days and their 2nd game against the Wizards.

The Pistons were able to control Monday’s game from start-to-finish, but the game was a little closer than it should have been because they had no answer for Anthony Davis.  Davis finished the game with 44 points and only missed 5 shots total.

The Pistons will still be without Jalen Duren, so they once again may struggle to guard Anthony Davis.  But, as Monday proved, even if they can’t stop Davis, they can still win if they stop the rest of the team.

Game Vitals

Where:  Capital One Arena in Washington DC
When:  Thursday, November 12 at 7 pm EST
Watch:  Scripps Sports Network
Odds:  Pistons (-10.5)

Analysis

There isn’t a ton more to say about this matchup that wasn’t very evident in Monday’s game.  With Jalen Duren out, the Pistons have no solution to opposing big men with any kind of offensive skill that are over 6’10”.  It seems hyperbolic, but it really has been the case.  Paul Reed is undersized and John Collins is not a natural center.  Tolu Smith has the size to possibly keep up, but he has proven to be out of his element pretty much any time he has gotten playing time so far.

The Pistons did opt to start John Collins at center against the Wizards on Monday and it did work out offensively, as he had a season-high 24 points.  But, the aforementioned Anthony Davis was able to cruise to 44 points without much resistance.  Anthony Davis always seems to have his best games against the Pistons and I wouldn’t expect him to hit a couple threes every single night, but a lot of the offense he was able to generate was off of offensive rebound putbacks or shots over the undersized players guarding him.

Surprisingly, the Pistons were only outrebounded 46-45, but they were outrebounded 14-11 on the offensive glass.  If you watched the game, you could see the Pistons lack of size rear it’s head countless times.  It is just the current state of things and something the Pistons will have to manage as best as they can for the next two weeks while Jalen Duren is still out with his hamstring injury.

The Pistons benefitted heavily from poor games out of Alex Sarr and Kyshawn George, which George in particular has been arguably the Wizards 2nd best player this season.  Trae Young also had a poor night from beyond the arc where he shot 3-of-10.  Some of that is because of how good the Pistons perimeter defense is and if the Pistons can replicate that tonight, it doesn’t really matter if they have nobody to slow down Anthony Davis.

AJ Dybantsa was able to get going a bit on Monday as he scored 21 points on 8-of-17 shooting.  There were times where he looked overwhelmed, as he had 5 turnovers, but he showed why he was the number 1 pick and a building block for the Wizards.  The Pistons have perimeter players to slow him down, but the refs were very whistle-happy on Monday which helped Dybantsa get momentum on his drives to the basket since the Pistons were not able to be as physical.

One small point of concern has been the play of Cade Cunningham over the last few games.  He had arguably his best game of the season a little over a week ago against the Charlotte Hornets and since then has really struggled, especially from beyond the arc.  He is 1 for his last 19 from beyond the arc after being close to 40% through the first seven games of the season.

He is playing more off-ball and getting clean looks, they just aren’t falling right now.  Teams are obviously focusing their defense more on Cade, but a lot of the current issues are just due to not being able to hit his outside shots.  Hopefully that changes tonight.

Luckily, Daniss Jenkins has been able to step up the last couple nights as he had a career-high, 31 points against the Lakers on Sunday and then 22 points, 6 rebounds, and 8 assists on Monday while starting.  Given the success the Pistons had starting him along with John Collins at center, I would suspect that they roll out that starting lineup again.

There were some issues defensively, which I already touched on, but the offense was much better with Collins starting and more-importantly, it finally got John Collins going after his early-season struggles.

If the Pistons are able to replicate the game they played on Monday, they shouldn’t have a difficult time defeating the Wizards, but if they let one of the other players besides Anthony Davis get hot, the Wizards have a shot at the upset.

Lineups

Detroit Pistons (7-3):  Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins, Duncan Robinson, Ausar Thompson, John Collins

Washington Wizards (4-8):  Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis, Alex Sarr

Question of the Day

Do you think there is a solution to the Pistons big-man struggles or do they just need to ride it out until Jalen Duren returns?

For those of you DBB sickos who care, I’m officially a married man! We had a spooky wedding on Halloween night and spent the past week in Cabo San Lucas for our honeymoon. We had a great time celebrating over the past week and a half!

Now we’re back to Pistons hoops.

JB Bickerstaff decided to mix up the starting lineup by starting John Collins at center. Paul Reed moved to the bench, and Daniss Jenkins was inserted into the starting lineup. Detroit started small with Duncan Robinson at the 3 and Ausar Thompson at the 4.

It proved to be the right idea early, as Collins was the leading scorer for Detroit after the first quarter with nine points. The Wizards took a 32-31 lead heading into the second, behind 12 points from Trae Young and 11 from Anthony Davis.

Detroit struggled to have an answer defensively for AD, and this was another game where Detroit missed Jalen Duren’s physicality and inside presence. Davis had 30 points and eight rebounds at the halfway point while only missing one of his 11 attempts. The Pistons put up 37 points in the quarter with five different players scoring more than seven points. Collins led the way with 15, Duncan had 14, and Cade had 11 as Detroit held a 68-58 lead.

The third quarter was all about Daniss Jenkins. Cade picked up his fifth foul halfway through the third, and DJ took the reins. He made Trae Young look like a traffic cone on defense as Jenkins went on to score 13 in the quarter. He consistently attacked Young, and Young never stood a chance. Detroit continued to extend their lead as they were up 103-87 heading into the fourth.

The fourth quarter was highlighted by two beautiful plays by Ebuka Okorie and Ausar Thompson.

First, watch Ausar find Okorie in transition as Okorie does his best Kyrie Irving impression:

AUSAR TO EBUKA WE ARE IN HEAVEN pic.twitter.com/jggv5WFEeC
— Rip Haminkton (@RedAlternates) November 10, 2026

Second, the Human Swiss Army knife blocks the 7-footer Alex Sarr on one end, then follows that up by directing traffic and finding an open DJ with a great bounce pass for a wide-open dunk:

Just let Ausar do everything pic.twitter.com/3nlVa0IHKi
— Rip Haminkton (@RedAlternates) November 10, 2026

The Pistons will continue to hope for a speedy recovery for Jalen Duren as they needed his inside physicality against Anthony Davis, who finished with 44 points and 13 rebounds while shooting 16-for-21 from the field. Detroit still managed to pull away with a 122-111 win behind three different players who scored 20+ points, despite none of them being Cade Cunningham.

John Collins, in his starting small-ball five role, led the way with 24 points and 10 rebounds, shooting 9-for-13 from the field. Both Daniss Jenkins and Duncan Robinson added 22 points each, and Jenkins led Detroit with eight assists. Your fun fact of the night: Robinson led the Pistons with seven free throw attempts. There has been a clear difference in his game this year as he looks to get to the line more often. Cunningham added 17 points and seven assists.

The Pistons improve to 7-3 on the season. Detroit’s home-and-home matchup with the Wizards continues as the Pistons will travel to Washington for Round 2 on Thursday night.

Go Stones.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Lakers: Austin Reaves pulls a Doncic to beat Detroit
pistons.body:
DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 8: Austin Reaves #15 of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket during the game against the Detroit Pistons on November 8, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Sevald/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

Who needs Luka Doncic when you have the US equivalent from Newark, Arkansas, Austin Reaves? The Los Angeles Lakers guard scored a game-high 43 as his MVP-level teammate rested with a back injury, propelling LA past the Detroit Pistons 121-116.

Honestly, the game had no reason to be as close as it was in the end. The Lakers led 40-14 one basket into the second quarter courtesy of insane shotmaking (hitting 72% from the floor) and an insane amount of Pistons miscues, including having more turnovers (eight) than made baskets (six).

But the Pistons, being the Pistons, weren’t about to give up. While Detroit pulled within one point early in the fourth quarter, the Lakers led wire to wire. So while it was only marginally competitive from Detroit’s point of view, it was certainly an instructive game. Here are some of the things I learned:

1. Kevin Huerter

Kevin Huerter is going to be a critical component of the Pistons’ rotation this season. In a game where Detroit’s entire backcourt didn’t really show up to play (both Cade Cunningham and Duncan Robinson were largely no-shows until some fourth-quarter scoring), Huerter was by far the biggest bright spot for the Pistons.

It also happened to be his best game in a Detroit uniform. Huerter hit four three-pointers, scored 24 points overall, and added five rebounds, five assists, five blocks(?!) and two steals. Ever since the Pistons traded for him at the deadline last season, it was clear Huerter makes winning plays, and you were hoping he’d be able to combine that with rediscovering his 3-point shooting stroke from earlier in his career. The early returns indicate the shot might be back, as well as everything that goes with it. After tonight, he’s hitting 40% from deep this season.

2. John Collins and Paul Reed

Detroit’s starting front court simply does not work, and it will never work. For as long as Jalen Duren remains sidelined or off the floor this season, this is going to be a significant issue for the Pistons. Duren is ramping back up from a hamstring injury and will be out two more weeks. Detroit has been, and will continue to be able to weather that storm. But it ain’t pretty, and any additional time off from Duren will have me significantly worried.

Most will want to pin the blame on the newcomer John Collins, and he has certainly played worse than Reed, but I think it’s the combination that brings out the worst in both players. Each is the kind of big man that relies on the gravity from teammates that allows them to use their athleticism to create the chaos that makes them effective. With both of them on the floor, it’s two bouncy balls pinging around the floor with no semblance of a plan on how to actually get the ball to the rim. The defense is also bad, and the rebounding is even worse. It’s an ugly situation, and it was exacerbated tonight by both men getting out-physicaled by the behemoth seven-footer Walker Kessler. Kessler, the Lakers’ big offseason addition, had 12 points and 16 rebounds, including seven on the offensive end. The Lakers also dominated the Pistons in the paint, 58-46.

Again, the lion’s share of the blame goes to Collins. He’s been quite bad all season, and it’s getting less clear by the day how he’s going to turn it around and be a positive force for the Pistons. I don’t think he’s ever met a 50-50 ball he couldn’t surrender to the opposition. But the pathway to him playing well lies with sharing the floor with Duren. Get well soon, JD.

3. Austin Reaves

The Pistons were correct in trying to give Austin Reaves the bag this offseason. Detroit reportedly was ready to give the wing a max contract this offseason as the second scorer and potential missing piece in a Detroit Pistons title run. Once the Lakers believed the pending RFA had a max offer on the table, they quickly moved to get an agreement to sign him on the eve of free agency so he’d never hit the market.

Reaves was insane tonight. The degree of difficulty on his shots begged belief. He was able to create space, get balanced, and score at all three levels. It was a sight to behold, and he was by far the best player on the floor for either team tonight.

4. Daniss Jenkins

Daniss has that dog in him, especially under two scenarios: 1. There is an impending buzzer. 2. He feels like his team is getting punked. Jenkins was truly the other hero of the game behind Huerter. He hit yet another buzzer-beater tonight, and he scored a career-high 31 points. When the Pistons were down huge, Jenkins got that look in his eye, as if to say, “This is not going to happen.”

From there, Jenkins started firing away from deep, and he was hitting. In the end, he canned eight three-pointers. He was also the ONLY Pistons player to go to the free-throw line more than once in the game. Really, Jenkins is like a better version of Marcus Sasser. He’s got scoring in his blood, and he’s more of an off-guard than a point guard, despite being stuck in a point guard’s body. He’s got three inches on Sasser and better floor vision, so he’s better overall and can cosplay as a point guard better than Sass, but Jenkins works best in this Pistons lineup when he’s not running the offense.

4. The refs.

The referees love the Lakers. Nothing else needs to be said.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs Lakers preview: Best Defense vs best offense
pistons.body:
Does it get any better than the No. 1 offense versus the No. 1 defense? The Detroit Pistons find themselves in that matchup as the 122-point-per-game Los Angeles Lakers visit Motown tonight.

Luka Dončić and the Lakers put up plenty of buckets, but scoring on Detroit is still an impossible task. The Pistons only surrender 101 points a game. Smothering defense every night.

Detroit’s defense has its biggest test of the season if Dončić suits up this evening. He’s questionable with lower back tightness.

It would be a shame if we’re robbed of Cade Cunningham going head-to-head with another MVP candidate. The bigger shame would be if we miss out on Dončić versus Ausar Thompson. That matchup is like Jerry Rice versus Deion Sanders with how both are operating.

GAME VITALS

Where: Little Caesars Arena, Detroit, MI

When: 6 PM EST

Watch: TV20 Detroit/DAZN-DET

Odds: Pistons (-4.5)

Analysis

Detroit hasn’t played since Wednesday’s loss to the Philadelphia 76ers. They’ve had plenty of time to rest up. They’ll need it if Dončić suits up.

Dončić is averaging 40 points. He’s shooting 42% on nearly 14 3s a game. He gets to the line more than anybody. It’s basically no stopping Dončić at the moment. This is a Wilt Chamberlain-like hot streak. Those two are the only players to average 40 nine games into the season. Whew, to say he’s balling is an understatement.

But tasks like this are why the Pistons employ Ausar Thompson. If *anybody* can slow Dončić down, it’s the best perimeter defender on the planet. Dončić usually has success against quick defenders with wiry strength, but Ausar is bigger and stronger this season. We’ll be keeping tabs on how Ausar takes Dončić’s bumps tonight. Ausar has the quick hands to disrupt things as well.

This might be a game where we see Paul Reed getting to the level and blitzing a bunch. J.B. Bickerstaff may decide to get the ball out of Dončić’s hands and force someone else to beat them. Reed is capable of coming to the level on screens and muddying things up.

I’m sure Dončić will see some Cade tonight too. Cade won’t make it easy with his sturdy frame. On the other end, the Lakers only have a few perimeter defenders to throw at Cade.

Matisse Thybulle is firmly in LA’s rotation as he’s started all 10 games. He’s still a defensive playmaking threat. Cade deals with defenders like this nightly, but Thybulle is a plus defender nonetheless. So is Ziaire Williams. The springy 25-year-old treats every possession as if he’ll never get in the game again if he doesn’t go hard.

Those two are solid defensively, and Jake LaRavia competes. Outside of that, Detroit will have plenty of favorable matchups (Walker Kessler is a great rim protector and is off to a good offensive start. He can make a difference).

Dončić displays effort and is trying to shake the terrible defender narrative on his name, but attacking him is still the best way to slow him down. Make him work and keep him involved in actions.

Austin Reaves falls into the same boat. He’s under Dončić on the Lakers’ best defenders on the team list. Anybody with that matchup should look to be aggressive.

Reaves spends most of his time covering shooting guards. Will JJ Redick make Reaves chase Duncan Robinson all night? That’s probably not ideal. Robinson runs even great defenders into the ground.

Robinson’s light-em-up stretch continues as he’s fourth in 3s made (35). Only Dončić, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, and Steph Curry have made more.

Detroit is letting it fly from deep as a team. According to Cleaning the Glass, 40 percent of their shots are coming from 3 (15th) compared to 31 percent last year (29th). Their rim rate has flipped the other way, but getting Jalen Duren back should rectify that.

The best offense versus the best defense is a mandatory viewing appointment. Can Ausar slow down the MVP-favorite? Do the Pistons show why they’re an elite defense and smother Dončić as a team? Does Cade deliver a masterclass against a guy he’ll be compared to for the foreseeable future if he’s in the MVP race? We’ll find out at 6 PM. Be there!

Projected starting lineup

Detroit Pistons (6-2): Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, Ausar Thompson, John Collins, Paul Reed

Los Angeles Lakers (8-2): Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia, Walker Kessler

pistons.headline: The Pistons go from owning to getting owned in the paint
pistons.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 04: Jalen Duren #0 of the Detroit Pistons looks on from the bench during a game against the Philadelphia 76ers at Little Caesars Arena on November 04, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

During a tumultuous playoff run and a prolonged offseason contract negotiation, Detroit Pistons fans were ready to say goodbye to Jalen Duren. Well, Duren has been out for six of eight games, and it turns out that Duren is the most indispensable member of the Pistons aside from Cade Cunningham.

A hamstring strain has knocked Duren out for six straight and counting, and boy, do you feel that every moment of every Pistons game.

Pundits and fans alike had easy diagnoses for what ailed the 60-win team during a disappointing second-round exit last season. Detroit needed a second scorer and much more perimeter shooting to succeed in the postseason. Its second-best player, the All-NBA big man Duren, couldn’t effectively operate in a congested, constipated offense when opponents had so much extra time to prepare their defense. That had a trickle-down effect on Cade Cunningham and on offensively limited players the Pistons relied on, like Ausar Thompson, Javonte Green, and Ron Holland.

This offseason, the Pistons seemingly tried and failed to add their second scorer (a planned run at Austin Reaves fizzled, and trade interest in players such as Kyrie Irving and Kevin Durant went nowhere). But they certainly addressed the team’s lack of perimeter punch. Detroit added guys such as Isaiah Joe, John Collins, and Taurean Prince. They re-signed midseason acquisition Kevin Huerter. They reformulated their offensive game plan to create more movement, space, and offensive responsibility among their non-Cade players. So far this season, the perimeter offense has hummed. Detroit is a top-10 team in 3-point shooting and almost middle of the pack in attempts despite Isaiah Joe missing most of the season to injury.

Detroit is 6-2, losing to the New York Knicks and on Wednesday night to the East-leading Philadelphia 76ers. Calls after both games from fans and casual watchers immediately turn to the team’s lack of that second star as the biggest issue. While that still might be a deal-breaker in the players, I would argue that the actual biggest issue in the season’s first eight games is Detroit’s collapse in its former ability to absolutely own the paint.

In other words, it’s not the lack of a Kyrie or a Durant or a Devin Booker. It’s the lack of Duren.

Last season, Detroit led the NBA in points in the paint, mostly behind Duren’s elite rim gravity and chemistry with Cade Cunningham and Detroit’s other ball handlers. Last season, the Pistons led the NBA with 57.9 points in the paint and were fourth in opponents’ paint scoring. They had a scoring differential inside of 14.2 points per game.  This season, Detroit ranks just 22nd in the paint at 44.8, down 13.1 points per game.

Rim gravity, it turns out, is just as important as perimeter shooting in creating the space needed to run a successful offense.

Paul Reed is a dynamic scorer inside, and he has some pop to his game. But he isn’t a rim runner like Duren. You give it to him on the block, and you let him work his magic. John Collins is opportunistic in transition, but those opportunities are dried up when he is the only big on the floor applying rim pressure, usually trying to duck in from the corners.

Ausar has the ball in his hands more, and it is working to create opportunities from others on the perimeter, but it is taking away a lot of those dunker-spot opportunities and back cuts that Thompson feasted on last season.

The lack of inside pressure is manifesting in other ways. Detroit has gone from a top-5 team in second-chance points to 22nd. They are 28th in offensive rebounding. Last season, they were third.

This team needs Jalen Duren back ASAP. And I think fans need to start reckoning with how crucial he is for this team to succeed.

lions.headline: Lions Week 10 preview: Breaking down Patriots’ offensive, defensive schemes
lions.body:
Sep 20, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel reacts in the seond half of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The Detroit Lions (6-2) and New England Patriots (5-4) are headed to Munich, Germany for a Week 10 battle between interconference opponents. Despite coming off a Super Bowl appearance in 2025, the Patriots’ season has been wildly inconsistent, looking unbeatable at times and completely vulnerable at others. While it’s impossible to know which Patriots team will show up on any given week, the Lions expect New England at their best in this matchup.

“Real good team here,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said of the Patriots. “I know the record is not the true indication of what this team is. There’s a number of things that go into that. […] You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they’re a good team. They’re dangerous. And they’re going to clean a lot of things up.”

Former Patriots quarterback and current color commentator Tom Brady covered the Patriots’ last game against the Packers—a 45-27 blowout—and he was less kind in his assessment of the Patriots:

“Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven’t turned the ball over, they haven’t exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it’s just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven’t quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error.”

Let’s take a closer look at the Patriots’ coaching staff, the scheme they run, and scouting notes from their most recently viewed games.

Patriots head coach: Mike Vrabel

Head coaching seasons: 8 seasons (Patriots 2025-present, Titans 2018-23)
Defensive coordinator: 1 season (Texans, 2017)
NFL coaching seasons: 13 seasons (Patriots, Browns, Titans, Texans)
NFL player seasons: 14 seasons (Chiefs, Patriots, Steelers)
Other coaching roles held: LB coach, DL coach, Consultant (Browns, 2024)
Influences: Bill Belichick, Romeo Crennel, Bill Cowher
Coached under: Crennel (DC), Bill O’Brien (HC)
Play caller: No

Dan Campbell on Patriots coach Mike Vrabel:

“I think Vrabel’s a hell of a coach”

Offensive coordinator: Josh McDaniels

NFL coaching seasons: 25th season (Patriots, Raiders, Rams, Broncos)
Head coaching seasons: 4 seasons (Raiders 2022-23, Broncos 2009-10)
Offensive coordinator seasons: 16 seasons (Patriots 2025-present, 2012-21, 2006-08, Rams 2011)
Previous coaching positions: QB coach, assistant
Influences: Bill Belichick, Charlie Weis, Nick Saban
Coached under: Belichick, Mike Vrabel, Steve Spagnuolo (Rams), Saban (Michigan State)

Offensive scheme

Passing game: Pro style
Running scheme: Downhill inside zone scheme
Scouting notes:

11 personnel is the primary set (60%)

12 personnel has seen an increase in recent seasons (24%)

13 personnel is less than 4%, despite rostering and playing four tight ends

21 personnel features both two-RB and RB+FB sets (8%)

Scheme staples: shotgun (58%), pre-snap motion, RPO, rollouts, screens, adaptable game plans

Play-action has been a staple in the past but has seen a reduction under QB Drake Maye

Play-action rate: 20.4% (23rd in the NFL) — Maye’s EPA using play-action: -0.28 (37th)

When the offense clicks, they can move the ball: 369.4 yards per game (8th), 6.0 yards per play (5th)

Turnovers have been an issue all season: -1.2 turnover differential per game (31st)

Interceptions have been a problem for Maye: 11 (tied for most in the NFL)

3 first-half INTs against the Packers: 1) communication; 2) threw into traffic; 3) telegraph

4th turnover vs. Packers: Fumble in the second half by RB Rhamondre Stevenson

Injuries on the offensive line have led to problems in protection

Pressures allowed: 141 (28th); pressure rate: 42.9% (31st); time to pressure: 2.78 seconds (29th)

Sacks allowed: 20 (17th); rate: 6.6% (18th)

Maye is very comfortable against the blitz: 0.03 EPA (14th); and pressure: -0.o4 (4th)

Maye navigates the pocket very well and uses designed rollout to get better looks when pressured

WR AJ Brown has been the top target (22% target share) when healthy, but he hasn’t been healthy most of the season and is currently injured

Watch out for TE Hunter Henry, who only sees a 14% time share (4th on team) but has the second-highest total EPA amongst the skill players

Run game is a priority but has underwhelmed

Middle-of-the-road rankings in most statistical categories

Success has come in yards after contact: 3.44 average YAftC (4th best)

Rush inside on 58.6% of run plays, 4th most in the NFL

Starting RB Rhamondre Stevenson is their best option, but he is dealing with an injury

RB2 TreyVevon Henderson has underperformed and has already been declared out.

Dan Campbell on Patriots offense:

“Josh (McDaniels) and those guys have done a hell of a job. Drake (Maye) is, I mean, he’s as good as they come getting out of the pocket right now. I mean, he’s very, very dangerous. Buying time, these five-plus-second throws, he’s dangerous. And then the skill he’s got around him, (WR DeMario Douglas) three and (WR Kyle Williams) 18, and then they got (WR Mack) Hollins back now and (TE Hunter Henry) the tight end. So, it’s potent. It is very potent. We got our hands full.”

Defensive coordinator: Zak Kuhr

NFL coaching seasons: 7th season (Patriots, Giants, Titans)
Defensive coordinator seasons: 2nd season (interim in 2025)
Previous roles: Inside LB coach, defensive assistant, quality control
Influences: Mike Vrabel, Shane Bowen (Giants DC 2024)
Coached under: Vrabel, Bowen, Brian Daboll (Giants)
Lions coaching staff connections: Assistant HC Terrell Williams (former Lions DL coach)

Defensive scheme

Base: Balanced 34 hybrid (Belichick system)
Coverage: Cover-1 Man Free, Cover-2/3/4 Zone — off-cover corners/split-zone safeties
Scouting notes:

Base 34: 21.5% usage

Nickel 24: 77.7% usage — second-highest usage in the NFL

Heavy blitz rate: 40.1% (6th) — hyper-aggressive in these situations

Blitzes are mostly straight down the middle with a Cover-3 look in the secondary

Non-blitz = stunts and twists get mixed in

Pass rush is their best weapon right now

Pressures: 120 (10th); rate: 37.3% (9th); time to pressure: 2.62 (13th)

Sacks: 25 (9th); rate: 7.8% (5th)

Pass rushers are athletic on the edge, and their interior defensive tackles can win one-on-one

However, at their core, they have a “stop the run first” mentality

Rush yards allowed per game: 96.7 (9th); per play: 3.9 (9th)

Yards before contact: 0.57 (3rd); yards after contact: 3.31 (24th)

Allow an explosive play on 12% of run plays (20th) — typically when teams attack the edges

Teams run outside on Patriots 53.8% (10th highest rate)

Man-Heavy secondary (36%), mainly Cover-1 Man Free — single-high with “Free” player used situationally

Zone schemes are balanced: Cover-2 (22%), Cover-3 (23%), Cover-4 (19%)

The secondary was supposed to be their strength, but they’re struggling, especially of late

EPA per pass yards allowed for the season: 0.07 (26th)

EPA per pass allowed over last four games: 0.35 (31st)

Explosive passes allowed: 7.2% (30th)

Lots of off-coverage and split-zone busted assignments against the Packers and Bears

Dan Campbell on Patriots defense:

“Defensively, they’re kind of a lot like us, man. They don’t want you to run the ball on them. They’re going to make sure that they stop the run. They are disruptive. They’re long. They got versatility at the D-line. Man, there’s a wave of guys. They got two or three deep waves of guys that are good football players across the board that they create havoc. And then here comes the pressure; here comes a lot of sticky man coverage, make you make accurate throws with people in your face and make contested catches.”

lions.headline: Discussion: Which NFL trade do you wish the Detroit Lions had made?
lions.body:
Lions GM Brad Holmes speaks to the media on Tuesday, Jan.11, 2022, in Allen Park. Lions | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

The NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and the Detroit Lions made just a modest move. They sent a 2029 sixth-round pick for depth safety Andre Cisco. While Cisco had been taken out of the starting lineup for the New York Jets—who are sporting a solid duo of Dane Belton and Mikah Fitzpatrick at the position—he comes to Detroit with plenty of playing experience and a knowledge of their system, having played under Aaron Glenn. It appears Cisco will have a role quickly with the team.

“We would like to get him going ASAP,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said Wednesday. “We’d like to get him going. He’s obviously going out to Germany with them. Our plan is to get him going in this game and let him help us a little bit. How much? That’s not quite there yet, but we do have a plan for him to help us.”

For many fans, that move wasn’t enough to move the needle for the Lions. They were hoping for a bigger splash, and potentially some help at the linebacker and cornerback positions. So today’s Question of the Day is:

Which move made at the NFL trade deadline do you think the Lions should have made?

My answer: First, let me explain why I asked the question this way.

Many people are mad that the Lions didn’t go out and get a player like Riq Woolen, Zack Baun, or Donte Jackson. But it’s hard to get mad at a move no one made, because we don’t know what conditions were required to trade for those players. Were they even available to trade for? Did the Lions try aggressively to acquire one, but the team wasn’t offering them at a reasonable price? Did the Lions ignore those players completely because they didn’t view them as scheme fits?

It’s impossible to informatively critique the Lions for failing to make a move when we have zero reliable knowledge on what it would’ve taken to acquire those players. Those conversations feel like a waste of time and energy.

However, we do know the conditions it took to trade for players who were moved over the last few weeks. We know for certain that they were available for trade, and we know (around) what it would’ve cost Detroit to acquire said player. So, among the moves that were made over the past few weeks, which one appeals to you the most?

YOU CAN SEE THE FULL LIST OF TRADES MADE IN-SEASON HERE IN OUR TRACKER

Interestingly, since the Joey Porter Jr. trade over a month ago, there have only been a few defensive trades made:

Bears trade for DT Jeffery Simmons

49ers trade for DT DeForest Buckner

Jaguars trade for DT Davon Godchaux

Jaguars trade for S Jessie Bates

Bills trade for S Amani Hooker

Lions trade for S Andre Cisco

Then two trades that were agreed upon fell through: Bengals trading for EDGE Arnold Ebiketie and Broncos trading for LB Daiyan Henley.

So, essentially, zero trades were made at positions of need for the Lions. I saw many wishing they had traded for Henley (Broncos were going to spend a fourth and 2028 fifth-round pick for him), and at this point, it’s unclear why the trade did not go through.

I will say, I’m intrigued by the other safety moves that were made. I think Jessie Bates is a game-changer, but a second-round pick for a half-season rental is a bit pricey for a Lions team that is getting healthier at the safety position right now. Hooker is a younger option who is signed through 2028 and comes with reasonable price tags of $9.57 million in 2027 and $11.8 million in 2028. If the Lions don’t believe Kerby Joseph will be around beyond this year, this could’ve been a very savvy move for what amounted to a second-round pick with a fifth-round pick in return.

However, the trade I keep going back to is the Joey Porter Jr. one. I still think that’s a move I would’ve made (cost the Cowboys a sixth and a 2028 second-round pick). While Porter has struggled with injuries with Dallas, his play on the field has been as advertised. I thought he was a great scheme fit, and a potential long-term option for a position Detroit has struggled to find consistency at. I wrote more about why I thought the Lions should’ve traded for Porter Jr. back in October.

Which trade deadline move, that was actually finalized, do you think the Lions should have made? Share your thoughts in the comment section below.

lions.headline: Lions, Patriots Week 10 injury report: Jared Goff limited; DJ Wonnum returns to practice

Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) high-fives teammates at warmup ahead of the game between Detroit Lions and Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

The Detroit Lions (6-2) head to Germany in Week 10 to take on the New England Patriots (5-4), but before they travel overseas, they’ll hold two practices in Allen Park: a walkthrough on Wednesday and a standard practice on Thursday.

A walkthrough practice means that all participation levels are estimates from the coaching staff based on how the player would have participated in a traditional practice. So, with that in mind, let’s look at Wednesday’s injury report and get you up to date on what we know.

Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded.

Injured list updates

LB Jack Campbell (neck, IR) — determined to play football again

S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — injury evaluation clock started

S Thomas Harper (ankle, IR) — eligible to begin practicing at any time

Campbell was officially added to the Lions injured reserve list last Saturday, and while he continues to improve, his overall health and status with the team remain undetermined. That said, Campbell is reportedly determined to play football again and wants the team to “make sure the house is taken care of until [he] can get back.”

Estimated no practice

RB Sione Vaki (ankle) — downgraded to no practice

C Cade Mays (low ankle sprain)

CB D.J. Reed (hip)

Vaki popped up on Week 9’s injury report late in the week, and while he was given a questionable designation for the game, he was available and contributed in RB2 and starting special teams roles. The Lions may take things slowly with him this week, but unless he had a set back, he still has a chance to play in Germany.

Mays and Reed were both injured in Week 8, missed Week 9, and appear to be longshots to suit up in Week 10, according to Lions coach Dan Campbell.

“I don’t see Cade and Reed practicing today,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said on Wednesday. “I don’t see them practicing today. They have got a way outside shot of playing. Way, way, way outside shot.”

Juice Scruggs has been starting at center while Mays recovers, and the Lions have rotated corners to split snaps while Reed is sidelined. Last week, Rock Ya-Sin got the start and played the majority of the rotation, but Khalil Dorsey, Ennis Rakestraw, and recently promoted Nick Whiteside saw some situational work as well.

QB Jared Goff (chest) — New Injury

Goff took a few more shots against the Dolphins than he normally does, so this could be a light day for him to recover, as there have been no indicators that they’re worried about him missing this game. We’ll still have to wait until Thursday to get a better idea, but there’s no need to panic just yet.

St. Brown was injured in Week 8 and had limited practice time ahead of Week 9, but he didn’t appear limited in the game. With this week’s game in his mother’s home country, and all the charity work he’s done in Germany over the last two years, you can be sure he’s playing.

Branch just cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol only to show up on this week’s injury report with a new ailment. It’s not clear when he suffered this hip injury, as he played the entire game last Sunday, but like Goff, we’ll have to double check his status on Thursday before we can feel totally comfortable.

Joseph continues to make positive strides as he acclimates back to football, and the Lions are happy with his progress, but Campbell has already told the media that Joseph won’t play in Germany. The Lions don’t have to decide on his PUP status until next Tuesday.

RB Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring) — Upgraded after limited practice last week

lions.headline: Christian Mahogany back in at starting LG spot in Week 10
lions.body:
Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions offensive lineman Christian Mahogany (73) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

After being pulled from the starting lineup in Week 9 for a “rules violation,” Christian Mahogany is set to return to his starting left guard spot in Week 10, according to Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell.

“Mahogany is going to go out there (today), and he’s going to start with the first unit,” Campbell said at his Wednesday press conference.

Mahogany’s career got off to a delayed start after contracting mono and missing the first half of his rookie season. In his second year, he won the starting left guard job but broke his left leg during the season and struggled to find his footing after returning. Now, in year three, Mahogany once again won the starting role at left guard and, with his health issues kept at bay, found his groove and has been excelling—currently ranked the 13th-best guard in the NFL by PFF, including grading inside the top 10 as a pass blocker.

Ahead of Week 9, Mahogany broke an undisclosed team rule and was benched in the Lions game against the Dolphins. Miles Frazier stepped into a starting role and struggled right out of the gate, committing holding penalties, allowing pressure, and failing to generate drive in the run game. He settled in well in the second half, but several of the Lions’ first-half drives stalled or ended early because of the offensive line’s play.

Immediately after the game, Campbell told the media that Mahogany committed a team rule violation, and while he was benched for that game, it “doesn’t mean it stays that way.” On Monday, Campbell said the two had discussed the matter and that “we’re good” moving forward, adding that it’s now up to Mahogany to show he can put this mistake behind him.

In addition to disclosing that Mahogany will return to his starting role, Campbell also shared that “he was good this morning,” suggesting everyone is taking positive steps forward.

lions.headline: Film study: Andre Cisco’s fit and Sione Vaki’s expanded role
lions.body:
Detroit Lions edge rusher Derrick Moore (8) makes a catch against New York Jets safety Andre Cisco (8) during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

The NFL trade deadline came and went, leaving most of the Detroit Lions faithful underwhelmed, disappointed, and frustrated with Brad Holmes for not matching the impact-level trades of the Chicago Bears or the Minnesota Vikings. Count me as one of them. I had my wish list of defensive backs I thought Holmes should target.

The good news, however, is that the Lions did not come away empty-handed. In fact, the trade for safety Andre Cisco stabilizes the safety room for Kelvin Sheppard’s defense for the cost of just a 2029 sixth-round pick. At that price, Cisco is essentially a free acquisition with 59 career starts, 8 interceptions, and 4 forced fumbles.

Shortly after the news of the Lions trade for Cisco, coach Dan Campbell shared his thoughts on the safety:

“We’ve liked Cisco from afar, having played against him and then even in free agency when he was with Jacksonville coming out. He’s athletic, he’s versatile, he knows our system, he knows our verbiage (via his time with Aaron Glenn and the Jets), so we feel like this is a guy that can help us here a little bit. We’re excited.”

The key takeaway is that Cisco knows the Lions’ system and verbiage, making him a plug-and-play contributor in the Lions’ rotating use of defensive backs. The defense spent the first half of the season working through a flood of missed assignments and trust issues. Cisco’s familiarity with the scheme should reduce the likelihood of those fatal errors from creeping back onto the tape.

For this film study, I set out to learn about Cisco and how he fits on this Lions. I also reviewed the film from the Week 9 game against the Miami Dolphins for anything noteworthy.

Cisco plays Dan Campbell’s brand of football

The first thing that stood out in Cisco’s film is that he plays safety as an aggressor, with violence and resilience. In the Lions’ Week 3 home game against the New York Jets, Cisco played 66 defensive snaps and played through the whistle on each one of them. Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, and Isaac TeSlaa are known for their physicality and effort as blockers, but Cisco was up for the challenge and battled the Lions wide receivers all game.

Below, on the Lions’ first run play of the game, Cisco (No. 8) shows on tape his desire to deliver the hit at the point of contact rather than finesse the block.

On the second play below, Cisco matches St. Brown’s physicality and sustains his effort in the tight red zone to get in on the tackle.

It cannot be emphasized enough how big of an impact this level of physicality and effort will matter down the stretch, especially against Ben Johnson and the Bears’ run game.

Cisco is versatile on defense and reliable on special teams

Beyond effort and physicality, Cisco has always been known for his versatility. Although used primarily as a high safety, Cisco showed he can blitz when he took down Jared Goff for a 10-yard loss.

With Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph (presumably), and likely Chuck Clark set to take on most snaps at safety, Cisco will have to contribute on special teams. For the Jets this season, Cisco has logged 130 special teams snaps. After reviewing a sample of these snaps, the common role he was tasked with on both punt and kickoff coverage units was as a contain/safety/trail player, a sign of his ability to instinctively read, react, and reliably tackle as a last line of defense.

For example, below is Cisco on kickoff coverage, lined up as the “L1” outside player on the left side of the formation. Instead of aggressively engaging with the return, Cisco’s role is to read and react with outside-contain leverage. Once the returner makes his vertical cut through an inside alley, Cisco closes down to make the play.

At the end of the day, Brad Holmes upgraded the Lions’ safety room with a clear play style and schematic fit, with a wealth of starting experience in Cisco at a negligible cost. By the end of the season, I expect this move to garner strong approval from even the most frustrated Holmes critics. Don’t be surprised if Cisco also earns himself a spot on the Lions 2027 roster.

Vaki the offensive chess piece

Without bypassing the Miami game entirely, one play Drew Petzing dialed up shows the continued evolution of both the offensive scheme and Sione Vaki’s role.

As shown below, Vaki is lined up as a fullback/h-back directly in front of Jahmyr Gibbs and used as a lead blocker on the crack-toss sweep.

Expanding Vaki’s role to include a pseudo-fullback option opens up many different options for the Lions offense. For example, the “sidecar” or “offset full house” formation the Lions used so effectively against Brian Flores and the Vikings’ defense could be adapted to use Vaki in one of the previously used tight end roles, opening up a host of different run and pass concepts from the same look.

When Ben Johnson ran the Lions offense, one noticeable feature was multiple layers, with formations and plays building off each other and setting up defenses weeks in advance. This is the art of play calling and offensive design. Petzing is starting to show that same talent and ability as an offensive coordinator.

If this trend continues, this offense could have another gear we haven’t seen yet.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions scouting report: Do the New England Patriots have a Super Bowl hangover?
lions.body:
FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 08: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots looks on after losing to the Green Bay Packers 45-27 at Gillette Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) | Getty Images

For the first time since 2015, the Detroit Lions are heading overseas! The Lions have played only two international games in their history—going 1-1 in London, England—but this time they’re headed to Munich, Germany. Entering this matchup, they’ve won four straight games and want to keep that streak alive while claiming their first-ever win in Germany.

Detroit takes on the New England Patriots, who appear to be in a rough spot right now, losing two of their last three games and barely above .500. Coming off a Super Bowl appearance last season, New England is currently the seven seed in the AFC, and with injuries also piling up, they’ve got a lot to overcome to keep their playoff hopes alive.

Let’s take a deep look at the Patriots’ season so far as they head into Week 10.

New England Patriots

2026 season thus far (5-4)

Week 1: Lost to Seattle Seahawks 13-10
Week 2: Defeated Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3
Week 3: Lost to Jacksonville Jaguars 35-6
Week 4: Defeated Buffalo Bills 29-26
Week 5: Defeated Las Vegas Raiders 45-17
Week 6: Defeated New York Jets 26-19
Week 7: Lost to Chicago Bears 30-24
Week 8: Defeated Miami Dolphins 24-19
Week 9: Lost to Green Bay Packers 45-27

Offensive stats:

Quarterback Drake Maye has had a rocky performance after being an MVP finalist last season. He had a rough first month, throwing “meatball subs,” as the kids say nowadays. Maye played well but had an abysmal Week 9, throwing three interceptions. This season, Maye is averaging 253.6 yards per game with 18 touchdowns and 11 interceptions, tied for the league lead in interceptions.

The Patriots’ running game has been lackluster this season. Second-year running back TreVeyon Henderson is in a sophomore slump, compounded by injuries, with just 203 yards, a touchdown, and 3.9 yards per carry. Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson hasn’t been explosive either, averaging 3.9 yards per carry with 399 yards and two touchdowns—and he could be held out of this game with a knee tendon issue. The team has seen a little bit of life in third-string back Corey Kiner, who is averaging 4.9 yards per carry with 244 yards and a touchdown.

At receiver, it’s been an interesting ride: the Patriots traded for wide receiver A.J. Brown to be their top receiver after losing Stefon Diggs in free agency, and Brown has battled ankle injuries, playing in only three games with 101 yards on nine catches. The top receiver currently is DeMario Douglas, who leads the team in yards (434) and touchdowns (four). The Patriots also signed Romeo Doubs in free agency to a big contract, and he is currently on IR, though he will return this season—he’s got 261 yards and three touchdowns in 2026.

One reason for the running game struggles is injuries on the offensive line. The Patriots are without both starting guards, Mike Onwenu and Alijah Vera-Tucker, and now left guard Ben Brown will most likely miss this week’s game, according to head coach Mike Vrabel. PFF ranks them 19th in run blocking (62.7), which plays a big part in why the running backs can’t find success on the ground. With them not having success on the ground, that puts more pressure on Maye to air it out, and suddenly he’s turnover-happy, trying to make plays for the offense.

Defensive stats:

On defense, the front seven has done a solid job overall. EDGE Elijah Ponder leads the team with 7.5 sacks and is tied for fourth-most in the NFL. Defensive tackle Christian Barmore has 4.5 sacks while rookie EDGE Gabe Jacas has 3.0.

The secondary has been about average, as newly extended cornerback Christian Gonzalez has six pass deflections and a 51.4 PFF coverage grade. Former Lions cornerback Carlton Davis III has been doing well, with a 72 coverage grade. Nickelback Marcus Jones has played well, tied with Gonzalez for the team-leading six pass deflections, and earned a 59.5 coverage grade.

New England is allowing a 67.5 percent completion percentage, the third-highest in the NFL, and is just nine yards behind the Lions for most passing yards allowed this season (2,256), according to Next Gen Stats. They’ve allowed some big plays in the air, including 32 20+ yard passing plays (second-most) and seven 40+ passing-yard plays (tied for fourth-most). Despite the pass rush getting home, it isn’t getting there fast enough for the secondary to hold up its end of the bargain. With teams struggling to run against New England, they’ve had to air it out and risk that pressure, and the secondary has had its share of woes.

Injury notes

Key players ruled out: WR Romeo Doubs (IR), G Mike Onwenu (IR), G Alijah Vera-Tucker (IR), LB Harold Landry III (PUP)
Key players to monitor: WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness), LT Will Campbell (knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee), LG Ben Brown (knee)

Injuries have started to pile up for the Patriots over the past few weeks. It started after Week 1 when A.J. Brown suffered an ankle injury and went to IR. He has returned from IR but has played only two games, as the injury is still bothering him. He has missed the last two games and, according to Tom Pelissero, should return sooner rather than later, perhaps after the Week 11 bye.

In his absence, Doubs and Mack Hollins stepped up but also suffered injuries: Hollins just returned from IR in Week 9, while Doubs is set to return from IR after the team’s bye week. The interior offensive line has seen both starting guards, Onwenu and Vera-Tucker, land on IR, with Vera-Tucker likely returning this season, though Onwenu’s status remains up in the air. New England is still waiting to activate linebacker Harold Landry III off PUP as well.

Week 9 was a bad week for New England injuries, starting with Henderson having a medical emergency that forced him to miss the game; his status is unknown. On the field, the Patriots saw four starters go down, all with knee injuries. Left tackle Will Campbell, Stevenson, Davis III, and Brown all left the game and didn’t return with their injuries. Campbell told the media after the game that he’s fine, while Vrabel didn’t provide an update on Stevenson or Davis III on Monday.

Biggest strength: Front seven

New England’s defense has been helping this team a lot, especially in stopping the run and getting to the quarterback. Starting with the pass rush, New England has 25 sacks overall, tied for ninth most in the league. Ponder has been playing lights out and has given this defense a big spark in their pass-rushing abilities. PFF grades them with an 82.8 pass rush grade, second-highest in the NFL.

Elijah Ponder closing out the first half with a SACK 😤@LVvsNE on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SFquxShY2n
— NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026

This front seven can do more than get to the quarterback; they can also slow down the running game. They’ve allowed an average of 3.9 yards per carry, tied for ninth-fewest. More impressively, though, they’ve allowed only one run over 20 yards, for 34. This team makes it really hard to run the football and dares you to drop back to throw it.

When you’re forced to air it out, that pass rush comes into play and pressures your quarterback. It’s a seesaw battle opposing offenses have to deal with. Do you go aggressive and try to run on them, or lean on your passing game to hopefully light it up? If the passing game succeeds, it opens the door for the run game to have a better chance of breaking one through; if you can’t do either, it’s going to be a long day for your offense.

Biggest weakness: Offensive injuries

While the data and numbers show the Patriots offense is average to slightly above average, injuries are piling up on that side of the ball. Maye has barely had his top two wide receivers together, and now possibly both of his top two running backs could be missing time as well. It doesn’t help that the team is already down two starting guards, and one of their replacements won’t be playing. Campbell has been playing great at left tackle, so if he somehow misses this game, it could really hurt New England’s chances at winning.

Maye hasn’t been consistent, and it’s hard when you don’t have all five starters in front of you for protection and your top weapons on the sidelines. New England has leaned on him to help with ground-game struggles, but with Hollins and Douglas as the top receivers, it’s tougher to expect much production than with Brown and Doubs. Maye is doing all he can, but he’s taken a step back from last season.

These injuries are piling up, and sure, some of the players will return and aren’t gone for the year, but if they don’t return soon, there might be nothing left to play for when they do. The AFC isn’t as dominant as the NFC, so New England can afford a few losses, but you don’t have an avalanche to start, and suddenly it’s December and fans are waiting for the 2027 NFL Draft in April.

Key matchup: Lions ground attack vs. Patriots front seven

This matchup will likely determine who wins this football game. While Detroit’s ground attack hasn’t had many big plays yet, the longest being a 30-yard rush, it’s still a strong part of who they are as an offense. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is having a solid season and making his case for MVP consideration. Detroit averages 4.4 yards per carry and has found the end zone 10 times on the ground.

I mentioned earlier how the Patriots’ run defense has been solid, and this will be a good-on-good battle. Detroit has a plethora of weapons in the passing game, and they can win through quarterback Jared Goff if need be. Against the Packers last week, the Patriots allowed 372 passing yards, and Detroit’s strong passing attack could give the Patriots secondary PTSD. While Detroit can lean on the passing game, that doesn’t mean it wants to, and it will keep trying to run the ball on this Patriots front seven. If Detroit can break through this unit and move the ball on the ground, that opens the door for the passing game to find success too.

If New England holds its ground and keeps opposing running backs down, Detroit could run into trouble. In their two losses, Gibbs totaled 98 rushing yards and only one touchdown on the ground. Detroit’s offense can survive a rough Gibbs game, but we haven’t seen them do it so far in 2026. If the Patriots can contain Gibbs, Detroit could have a long flight home.

Vegas line for Sunday: Lions favored by 2.5

lions.headline: For the Detroit Lions, ugly wins are a thing of beauty
lions.body:
Nov 8, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell celebrates with defensive back Brian Branch (32) after an interception during the second half against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Winning the ugly ones is just as important as the pretty ones—they count the same in the standings, after all—and that’s where the Detroit Lions need to keep pace with an NFC North that refuses to ease up. For yet another week, everyone in the Black and Blue division with a quarterback capable of performing the forward pass picked up wins. It’s maddening, it’s odds-defying, it feels like it has to let up at some point, but until it does, winning is all that matters for this Lions team.

Most of the noise on game day centered on the new guy at left guard, Miles Frazier, stepping in for starter Christian Mahogany. In real time, people scrambled to find an explanation. Was Mahogany hurt in pregame warmups? What were his PFF grades over the last three games? Did he catch the South Beach Flu? People hardly had enough time to investigate before Detroit took the field and mustered up a measly 110 yards and six points on offense in the first half. Prior to halftime, fans had lost their patience with Frazier’s performance. Jared Goff was sacked three times, Jahmyr Gibbs had four carries of zero or negative yards, and the Lions were up just three points at halftime against a 1-6 Miami Dolphins team.

Enough was enough: Mahogany needed to be put in at left guard to help the Lions offense get back on track.

Except that didn’t happen. Mahogany played just five snaps on Sunday in Miami, all of those opportunities coming on field goal kicks. The Lions offense turned things around just enough in the second half. Goff stayed upright, Gibbs broke into the end zone for the game’s only touchdown, and the Lions defense (!) made sure this one ended in a victory. Not for them, but for their leader, Jack Campbell, who had to watch his defense from a hospital room, still regaining his physical faculties—but determined to return to the field.

Social media was filled with videos and photos of the Honolulu Blue takeover at Hard Rock Stadium, fans chanting and holding signs in support of Campbell and the Lions. Your feed was filled with as much love and support as it was with people wondering how Mahogany’s crime could justify the time he spent on the sideline. Dan Campbell offered no further insight into the infraction immediately after the game, but has since alluded to the fact that Mahogany had broken team rules “multiple times.”

Dan Campbell made the right decision when it came to holding Mahogany accountable. There’s no room in their building for anyone to be above the standard, whether you’re a starter or a healthy inactive on game day. That isn’t a new sentiment—it’s been the foundation since the afternoon Campbell walked through the door.

“But I’ll guarantee you this: these guys are gonna fight, and they’re gonna scratch and claw, and they’re gonna be something this city is proud of because they’re going to take on the identity of this city,” Campbell said in his introductory press conference.

“It ain’t always going to be roses up here. ‘Everything’s gonna be the way that we all want it to be and look perfect,’ but I know this, man, we’re gonna fight, we’re gonna scratch, and we’re gonna claw, and I know the good teams find a way to get it done.”

Campbell told us it wasn’t always going to be pretty, and we’ve been reminded over these past couple of weeks just how ugly football can get, but there’s something beautiful in it all.

“If somebody goes down, the next one steps up, and he’s expected to produce enough to help those guys next to him when these guys are going to learn to play together, play for one another.”

From the disciplinary action against Mahogany to Jack Campbell’s absence in the middle of Detroit’s defense, from the offense’s struggles to Kelvin Sheppard’s unit getting the job done, Sunday was a testament to how they’ve become that good team Campbell referenced over five years ago. Their 6-2 record is a reflection of the image this football team was built on by Dan Campbell.

“It’s not about the best 53, it’s about the right 53.”

michigan.headline: Betting the Big Ten examines judgment day for USC, Northwestern, and Ohio State
michigan.body:
CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 16: Carnell Tate #17 of the Ohio State Buckeyes runs with the ball after a reception against the Northwestern Wildcats during the first half at Wrigley Field on November 16, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Week 10 was certainly an interesting one here on Betting the Big Ten. Michigan and Michigan State predictably hit the under, while UCLA and Wisconsin covered. We missed badly on the Ohio State vs. Oregon under, but I am A OK with that as the Ducks offense exploded for 41 points against the Buckeye defense. We finished the week 4-4, bringing our season total to 55-49-1. We’re still in the green!

Week 11 has a couple of do-or-die type games on the schedule as USC looks to stay alive against Indiana. Ohio State and Northwestern are likely already out of CFP contention, but the loser of that matchup won’t even have a prayer’s chance anymore. It could be an interesting week.

As always, all lines are courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook. Please bet responsibly.

Illinois at UCLA (-10), O/U 47.5, 9 p.m. ET Friday

If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it. UCLA is still unblemished on the season against the spread. Vegas still isn’t showing the Bruins the love, as the spread here has shifted from UCLA -13 to -10. Until proven otherwise, I’m always taking the Bruins.

The pick: UCLA -10

Northwestern at Ohio State (-12.5), O/U 45.5, Noon ET Saturday

This is a sneaky game that the Buckeyes could lose. However, it helps that it’s in Columbus. Per The Action Network, 61% of all bets are on Northwestern, yet the spread has slid from Ohio State -9.5 up to 12.5. There’s big money on the Buckeyes in this one, which is always difficult to bet against. Pay special attention to the health of Aidan Chiles this week.

The pick: Ohio State -12.5

Wisconsin (-8.5) at Maryland, O/U 43.5, Noon ET

According to The Action Network, a whopping 94% of all bets against the total in this matchup are on the over. You’d think that would mean the total would skyrocket up. Instead, it hasn’t moved an inch. While Maryland tends to go over (7-2), Wisconsin is just 3-6 against the total and has gone under in five straight games. That’s enough for me to ride the under.

The pick: Under 43.5

Nebraska (-14) at Rutgers, O/U 52.5, 12:30 p.m. ET

14 is an awkward spread in this one. The betting public seems to be split on it as well. There isn’t much to be gleaned on the total, as Nebraska is 3-6 and Rutgers is 6-3, so they are polar opposites. However, Matt Rhule’s Cornhuskers are 6-3 ATS while Rutgers is just 4-5. It’s not an incredibly strong trend, but I like Nebraska to break their outright losing streak in a big way this weekend.

The pick: Nebraska -14

USC at Indiana (-10), O/U 50.5, 3:30 p.m. ET

USC has to have this game in order to stay in CFP contention. You know what Lincoln Riley tends to do when he has to have games? He loses them. Despite 82% of the betting public being on USC this week, the spread took an abrupt jump from 7 to 10 in Indiana’s favor. Vegas knows something. I’m not sure what it is, but it’s something significant. Give me the Hoosiers.

The pick: Indiana -10

Michigan at Oregon (-10.5), O/U 38.5, 3:30 p.m. ET

Let’s get weird. Is Michigan any good? Absolutely not. Is Oregon any good? Maybe, but it might be too late for them. The total is untouchable here as Michigan nearly always goes under (2-7) while Oregon goes over a majority of the time (6-3). While both of these teams are below .500 ATS, there’s one trend that I love: Michigan is 2-0 ATS as an underdog while Oregon is a hideous 2-5 ATS as a favorite. Will Michigan win this game outright? Most certainly not as the Wolverine offense doesn’t know how to score. However, I love the Michigan defense when I can be given 10.5 points.

The pick: Michigan +10.5

Washington (-3.5) at Michigan State, O/U 43.5, 4:15 p.m. ET

Michigan State had been having an abysmal season prior to pulling out all the stops to beat Michigan in Ann Arbor last weekend. The Spartans ran an offensive scheme that they hadn’t shown all season and likely had been saving for their rivals. The week after is a prime letdown spot. This is still a not-very-talented MSU team, so I’ll take Washington and lay the points.

The pick: Washington -3.5

Minnesota at Penn State (-9.5), O/U 41.5, 7 p.m. ET

This is the most stunning spread of the week in my opinion. Minnesota had been one of the pleasant surprises of the Big Ten season with wins over Michigan and Iowa prior to losing to Indiana and UCLA in their last two games. Penn State had been the laughingstock of the conference as the Matt Campbell era was off to a brutal start. However, the Nittany Lions have won two games in a row over Purdue and Washington. Both are middling ATS, but the spread being this large is such a rat line. I’m eating the cheese.

The pick: Penn State -9.5

Purdue at Iowa (-17.5), O/U 47.5, 7:30 p.m. ET

Don’t look now, but Iowa is a dark-horse CFP contender. There’s a world where the Hawkeyes win out, finish 10-2 and third in the Big Ten, meaning they won’t pick up a loss in the final Big Ten Championship Game. It’s hard to imagine a 10-2 Big Ten team not making the CFP. Iowa is 6-3 ATS while Purdue is 3-6 and 1-2 ATS on the road. I’m nervous about this pick, but the Hawkeyes just have so much more to play for than Purdue does.

The pick: Iowa -17.5

michigan.headline: Recruiting Roundup: Michigan faces flip threat from SEC school for 4-star commit
michigan.body:
Zach Libby/Maize n Brew

Welcome to the Recruiting Roundup, our twice-per-week series breaking down the latest developments on the recruiting trail for the Michigan Wolverines. We’ll keep you up to date on the top targets, the visits they take, the predictions that analysts make, and everything in between. Here’s what you need to know today…

Ole Miss making a push for Michigan commit

Michigan has a recruitment to watch closely in its secondary, as flip predictions have been entered favoring 2027 four-star defensive back Tavares Harrington to flip to Ole Miss.

The Chicago Mount Carmel prospect committed to Michigan on May 22, choosing the Wolverines over a group of finalists that included the Rebels. Ole Miss has continued to pursue the 6-foot-3 defender and now appears to be a serious threat to pull him away.

Harrington remains committed to Michigan, but losing him would be another setback in the secondary after four-star safety Darrell Mattison flipped from the Wolverines to Ole Miss back in May.

The development comes as Kyle Whittingham’s staff works to reassure commitments following offensive coordinator Jason Beck’s dismissal. Whittingham said he and the staff reached out to every recruit and received positive responses.

“We got on the phone with every recruit (Sunday) night,” Whittingham said. “And they seemed to be very receptive and positive. Nobody was panicking.”

The Wolverines have work to do with Harrington. The predictions don’t make the flip official just yet, but they give fans reason to keep a close eye on this one.

Four-star edge commit remains solid despite Tennessee visit

Another Michigan commitment visited an SEC school over the weekend, but the circumstances should ease concerns about his future. According to Ethan McDowell of The Wolverine, 2027 four-star edge commit Ifeanyi Emedobi planned to return to Ann Arbor before a family obligation prevented the trip.

Instead, the Fort Wayne Northrop prospect joined a group from Traction Athletic Performance, where he trains, for Tennessee’s game against Kentucky. The Volunteers have not offered Emedobi and were not actively recruiting him at the time of McDowell’s report. Tennessee took his measurements and indicated the staff might reach back out to him, but he had not heard from the program afterward.

Even while in Knoxville, Emedobi was keeping tabs on Michigan’s game against Michigan State. A source close to his recruitment put it simply to McDowell:

“Ife loves Michigan.”

His relationships with defensive line coaches Lewis Powell, Larry Black and David Denham remain a major reason he feels comfortable with his pledge.

“Communication’s been great,” Emedobi said earlier this fall. “We talk every day of the week.”

Emedobi still plans to enroll at Michigan in January. McDowell’s assessment is that a coaching change along the defensive line would be the development that could give the Wolverines something to worry about. For now, the Tennessee trip doesn’t appear to have changed his plans.

Boston College DL commit impressed with Michigan

While working to retain its commitments, Michigan is also pursuing 2027 three-star Boston College defensive line pledge Jayden Paulino. According to 247Sports’ Brian Dohn ($), Paulino came away impressed with his visit for the Michigan State game after receiving a Michigan offer the previous week.

“It was a great experience,” Paulino said. “The staff was welcoming and amazing.”

The 6-foot-4, 270-pound New Jersey prospect looked beyond the loss, pointing to the campus atmosphere, facilities and the program’s potential under Whittingham. Michigan’s defensive performance also caught his attention, as did Black’s coaching style.

“Coach Black is a tough, energetic guy, and those are some characteristics I want any coach to have,” Paulino said.

Paulino remains committed to Boston College, which secured his pledge June 17, but he is exploring his options. Penn State is scheduled to host him for an official visit this weekend, while Missouri recently offered and Miami is showing interest.

A return visit to Michigan for the Nov. 21 UCLA game is also in the works, giving the Wolverines a potential opportunity to build on a strong first impression.

michigan.body:
ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 02: Nishad Strother #50 of the Oregon Ducks plays against the Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium on November 02, 2024 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The Michigan Wolverines suffered one of the worst losses in modern program history on Saturday, falling at home to the Michigan State Spartans, who came into the game sitting at 2-6 and on a six-game losing streak, 15-6.

I’ve floated the phrase “rock bottom” around a couple of times this year, but this is it. We’ve hit rock bottom, and now the Wolverines have to go on the road to take on the Oregon Ducks.

Last week, I predicted Michigan was going to lose to Michigan State because I didn’t think that Kyle Whittingham was going to get his team motivated for a rivalry game. The Spartans are a bad football team, but they clearly have a coach who is trying and who cares. Sure enough, both teams embodied their head coach in that game. Michigan was lifeless, unenthusiasic, and just flat out looked like a team that didn’t want to be there.

After the game, Michigan fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, which needed to be done. However, nothing will change until the Wolverines find a new head coach who embraces the program and actually wants to do his job. With a road test against a ranked team looming, things are only going to get worse. Here are a few predictions for this weekend’s contest against the Ducks:

Michigan will get shut out

We almost saw this happen last week at home against one of the worst teams in the Big Ten, so why should we expect a better performance out west against the Ducks? Players have checked out and the head coach doesn’t want to be here. The recipe going into this game could not be worse. Before the Michigan State game, things were bad, but a win would’ve made the Wolverines 6-3. And the losses, while painful and self-inflicted, were somewhat forgivable. However, there is no coming back from the atrocity we witnessed last weekend. It will only get worse.

Kyle Whittingham will be fired after the game

The one positive that will come from last week’s disaster is that I can’t see any scenario where Whittingham is Michigan’s head coach on Dec. 1. The fan base is now completely against him, and the program is at its lowest point in over a decade. It’s going to happen within the next month, and I think Saturday might be so bad that the school decides to get it over with before the end of the season.

Oregon wins 17-0

I think that the defense will once again do enough to put Michigan in a spot to win a football game, but the offense isn’t going to get it done. It will be another frustrating watch, but we will move one step closer to putting this dumpster fire of a season in the rearview mirror.
